findings.checklist_item: Correct AC#2 to scan for the tokens that actually exist (`DETACHED_PROCESS`/`CREATE_NO_WINDOW`, not `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP`) and scope the `start_new_session` check so it does not false-positive on the legitimate reap-based spawn sites (grounding/harness.py, acli_subprocess.py, wiki_render.py).
evidence: start_new_session=True is present at grounding/harness.py:174, acli_subprocess.py:442, wiki_render.py:390 for killpg reaping (per _proc.py docstring lines 3-7), unrelated to detached-rebar-child spawning
findings.finding: AC#2's static scan is specified against tokens that don't match the code: `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` appears nowhere in the repo (the actual Windows detach token is `DETACHED_PROCESS | CREATE_NO_WINDOW`), and `start_new_session` legitimately appears in three OTHER spawn sites that are NOT detached-rebar-child sites (grounding/harness.py:174, adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py:442, adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py:390), which _proc.py's own docstring names as reap_process_group consumers.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC#2 (STATIC test enforcing detach flags appear only in _proc.py)
scenarios: As written, the scan for CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP matches nothing (giving false confidence about the Windows branch), while a scan for start_new_session either fails against the three pre-existing killpg sites or silently needs an unstated allowlist — so a fourth copy-paste site could still slip past.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend AC2's static scan (or add an AC) so the durable-cwd wiring is also centralized/verified in _proc.py, not just the detach flags and PYTHONPATH bootstrap.
evidence: Scope: helper 'would own the PYTHONPATH bootstrap, the detach flags and the durable cwd'
AC2 scans only for 'the detach flags (start_new_session / CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP) and the PYTHONPATH bootstrap'
Provenance/Why-this-matters: the propagated defect was 'a missing cwd= on the detached Popen'
findings.finding: The static test AC (AC2) enforces centralization of the detach flags and PYTHONPATH bootstrap, but NOT the durable cwd — which was the exact property whose omission (bug 3198) motivated this consolidation. A fourth spawn site (or the consolidated helper itself) could omit cwd and still pass the static scan.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC2; Scope bullet ('It would own the PYTHONPATH bootstrap, the detach flags and the durable cwd')
scenarios: A future fourth detached-spawn site copies the helper call but a refactor drops the cwd wiring; static test still passes because it only checks detach flags + bootstrap.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'and the durable cwd (detached_child_cwd) application' to the AC2 static-scan set, and assert the helper passes an explicit cwd to Popen so a fourth site cannot re-introduce bug 3198.

findings.checklist_item: Confirm whether the repo_root cwd-fallback decision is scoped as a decision-record only (keep in this ticket) or, if it may become a behavior 'change', split the degraded-fallback implementation into its own child so the spawn-helper consolidation stays a single coherent refactor.
evidence: 'Related open question, deliberately NOT changed while fixing 3198: should _config_sources.repo_root's final Path.cwd() fallback DEGRADE rather than raise?'
'if the decision is 'change', the degraded fallback is implemented.'
The detached-spawn consolidation targets three detached-child call sites; the repo_root fallback targets a disjoint set of in-process daemon threads.
findings.finding: The plan bundles two distinct concerns: (1) consolidating the three detached-spawn sites behind `spawn_detached` (call sites: push.py, enrich_drain.py, compact_trigger.py), and (2) deciding+possibly changing `_config_sources.repo_root`'s cwd fallback for long-lived IN-PROCESS callers (daemon threads at _mcp_writes.py, editor.py, janitor.py, _heartbeat.py, config.py). These touch different subsystems and different call-site sets; if the repo_root decision is 'change', the degraded-fallback implementation is an independently-valuable, separately-releasable behavior change unrelated to the spawn-helper extraction.
findings.location: Scope — third bullet ('Related open question, deliberately NOT changed while fixing 3198') and AC line 4
scenarios: If the recorded decision is 'change', implementing the degraded repo_root fallback affects daemon threads that never spawn a detached child — a separate increment of value that could ship independently of the spawn-helper refactor.
A reviewer/claimant cannot close the spawn-consolidation slice green while the repo_root fallback implementation is still open, coupling two otherwise-independent outcomes.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the repo_root decision-recording here (comment + docstring), but if the decision is 'change', spin the degraded-fallback implementation out as a linked child ticket so this ticket remains the pure three-site consolidation.

findings.checklist_item: Add a behavioral test asserting `spawn_detached` re-raises the underlying failure (e.g. OSError) so each caller's existing except clause still catches it, verifying the 'no exception-surface change' claim rather than only the static flag-placement scan.
evidence: 'it RE-RAISES on failure — the never-raise posture stays per-caller, because the three sites do not catch identically'
'Each caller keeps its existing except clause and its own log line, so the refactor changes no exception surface.'
AC line 2 specifies only a STATIC test (source scan); no behavioral test of the re-raise/catch contract is named.
findings.finding: The plan's central safety claim — that folding spawn logic into `spawn_detached` while keeping per-caller `except` clauses 'changes no exception surface' — is asserted but not backed by any named behavioral test. The helper re-raises on failure so push.py (catches only OSError, logs %r) and drain/sweep (catch broad Exception, exc_info=True) each keep their distinct catch. The only named test is the STATIC source-scan (AC line 2), which checks WHERE flags appear, not that the helper actually re-raises so each caller's differing catch still fires.
findings.location: Scope — first bullet ('it RE-RAISES on failure … Each caller keeps its existing except clause') and AC line 2
scenarios: If `spawn_detached` swallows or wraps an error instead of re-raising the raw exception type, push.py's OSError-only catch would silently stop firing (broadening or narrowing its exposure) and no named test would catch the regression.
The 'changes no exception surface' claim closes green on the static scan alone while the runtime catch behavior has actually shifted.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a unit test that forces the underlying Popen to fail and asserts spawn_detached re-raises the original exception type, plus per-caller tests (or one parametrized test) confirming push.py catches OSError and drain/sweep catch broad Exception as before.

findings.checklist_item: Specify that spawn_detached must recompute the `src` PYTHONPATH root from _proc.py's own location (dirname applied 2x, not 3x) — or pass `src` in as a parameter — so the bootstrap points at src/ and not the repo root.
evidence: All three sites use `src = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))` (push.py:196, enrich_drain.py:426, compact_trigger.py:225)
_proc.py lives at src/rebar/_proc.py (one level shallower than src/rebar/_store/push.py), so dirname x3 from _proc.py resolves to the repo root, not src/
findings.finding: The PYTHONPATH bootstrap's `src` derivation (`os.path.dirname` applied 3x to `__file__`) is position-dependent and yields the wrong directory when moved into _proc.py: the three current sites (src/rebar/_store/push.py, src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py, src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py) are one directory deeper than _proc.py, so x3 gives `src/` for them but the repo root for _proc.py.
findings.location: Scope bullet: 'It would own the PYTHONPATH bootstrap, the detach flags and the durable cwd'
scenarios: Helper computes `src` from its own __file__ and puts the repo root on the child's PYTHONPATH; the bare-python child then cannot `import rebar` and dies at startup — the exact class of silent detached-child failure this plan exists to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: Have callers pass the already-correct `src` (or compute it as `os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))` from _proc.py) and note this explicitly in the Scope bullet.
